svg.title: How a Trajectory stores its motions
svg.desc: Animated: one AGV's trajectory as a timeline, as the std::set<Motion> it is stored in today (a balanced tree keyed by start time) and as a sorted std::vector; then three AddMotion calls: an append, an overlap that is rejected, and a second motion at the same start time, which is also rejected.
svg.metadata: ["A trajectory of four motions: a wait, two edges and a lift. On the timeline they abut (one ends when the next begins). std::set keeps them in a balanced tree keyed by start time, one heap node per Motion; a sorted vector would keep the same order in one contiguous block.", "AddMotion(m4, 13 s to 16 s), the case every AddMotion in CHUGG's sequential path takes: lower_bound finds no later motion, the last one (m3) ends at 13 s, so m4 goes at the end. In the tree it is a new leaf; in a vector it would be a push_back.", "AddMotion(x, 8 s to 12 s) overlaps m2 and m3. lower_bound stops at m3 (the first start at or after 8 s); x does not end before m3 starts, so AddMotion returns false and stores nothing. The callers in CHUGG ignore the return value, so a rejected motion would vanish silently.", "Same start time. y is a zero-length motion at 16 s and is accepted. z (16 s to 18 s) starts at the same time: operator< compares only start times, so y and z are equivalent keys, lower_bound returns y and AddMotion refuses z. SippAgv drops zero-length states, so CHUGG avoids this case.", "Summary: how CHUGG uses a Trajectory. Every insert is an append, the reads are in-order scans and the last element, and the one function that needs indexes copies the set into a vector first. The tree's strengths (cheap inserts in the middle, stable iterators) go unused."]

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: m0 to m4, x, y and z are an illustrative example. The behaviour of AddMotion, operator< (Interval::Before) and the call sites are from trajectory.hpp, trajectory.cpp, chugg_common.cpp, chugg_sequential.cpp, sipp_agv.cpp and coalesce_trajectory.cpp.

g.text: How a Trajectory stores its motions

text.font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

g.text: std::set is an ordered container: it does keep motions in time order. Its key is the start time alone, and AddMotion adds the no-overlap rule. Step through three inserts, then compare what the code needs with what each container offers.

text.font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
